celebration.title: In Transfiguratione Domini Nostri Jesu Christi

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, lábia + mea apéries.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, + open thou my lips.

segments.t: Dómine, lábia + mea apéries.

content.latin: ℟. Et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
content.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare thy praise.

segments.t: Et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.

content.latin: ℣. Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.
content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

segments.t: Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

segments.t: Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.

content.latin: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Allelúia.
content.english: Alleluia.

content.english: Ant. The Most High King, the King of glory, even Christ, * Him let us worship.

segments.t: Ant.
Summum Regem glóriæ, * Christum adorémus.

content.latin: Ant. Summum Regem glóriæ, * Christum adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Most High King, the King of glory, even Christ, * Him let us worship.

segments.t: Ant.
Summum Regem glóriæ, * Christum adorémus.

content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Ant. Summum Regem glóriæ, * Christum adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Most High King, the King of glory, even Christ, * Him let us worship.

segments.t: Ant.
Summum Regem glóriæ, * Christum adorémus.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Christum adorémus.
content.english: Ant. Him let us worship.

segments.t: Ant.
Christum adorémus.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

segments.t: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius
(genuflectitur)
veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.

content.latin: Ant. Summum Regem glóriæ, * Christum adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Most High King, the King of glory, even Christ, * Him let us worship.

segments.t: Ant.
Summum Regem glóriæ, * Christum adorémus.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Christum adorémus.
content.english: Ant. Him let us worship.

segments.t: Ant.
Christum adorémus.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: Quicúmque Christum quǽritis,
content.english: All ye who would the Christ descry,

content.latin: Oculos in altum tóllite:
content.english: Lift up your eyes to him on high:

content.latin: Illic licébit vísere
content.english: There mortal gaze hath strength to see

content.latin: Signum perénnis glóriæ.
content.english: The token of his majesty.

content.latin: Illústre quiddam cérnimus,
content.english: A wondrous sign we there behold,

content.latin: Quod nésciat finem pati,
content.english: That knows not death nor groweth old,

content.latin: Sublíme, celsum, intérminum,
content.english: Sublime, most high, that cannot fade,

content.latin: Antíquius cælo et chao.
content.english: That was ere earth and heaven were made.

content.latin: Hic ille Rex est géntium
content.english: Here is the King the gentiles fear,

content.latin: Populíque Rex iudáici,
content.english: The Jews' most mighty King is here

content.latin: Promíssus Abrahæ patri
content.english: Promised to Abraham of yore,

content.latin: Eiúsque in ævum sémini.
content.english: And to his seed forevermore.

content.latin: Hunc, et prophétis téstibus
content.english: 'Tis he the prophets' words foretold,

content.latin: Iisdémque signatóribus,
content.english: And by their signs shown forth of old;

content.latin: Testátor et Pater iubet
content.english: The Father's witness hath ordained

content.latin: Audíre nos et crédere.
content.english: That we should hear with faith unfeigned.

content.latin: Iesu, tibi sit glória,
content.english: Jesu, to thee our praise we pay,

content.latin: Qui te revélas párvulis,
content.english: To little ones revealed today,

content.latin: Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
content.english: With Father and blest Spirit One

content.latin: In sempitérna sǽcula.
content.english: Until the ages' course is done.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.english: Nocturn I

content.latin: Ant. Paulo minus * ab Angelis minorátus, glória et honóre coronátus est, et constitútus super ópera mánuum Dei.
content.english: Ant. Even while He was made a little lower than the angels, * He was crowned with glory and honour, and made to have dominion over the works of God's hands.

segments.t: Ant.
Paulo minus * ab Angelis minorátus, glória et honóre coronátus est, et constitútus super ópera mánuum Dei.

content.latin: Psalmus 8 [1]
content.english: Psalm 8 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 8

content.latin: 8:2 Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
content.english: 8:2 O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in the whole earth!

segments.t: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!

content.latin: 8:2 Quóniam eleváta est magnificéntia tua, * super cælos.
content.english: 8:2 For thy magnificence is elevated * above the heavens.

segments.t: Quóniam eleváta est magnificéntia tua, * super cælos.

content.latin: 8:3 Ex ore infántium et lacténtium perfecísti laudem propter inimícos tuos, * ut déstruas inimícum et ultórem.
content.english: 8:3 Out of the mouth of infants and of sucklings thou hast perfected praise, because of thy enemies, * that thou mayst destroy the enemy and the avenger.

segments.t: Ex ore infántium et lacténtium perfecísti laudem propter inimícos tuos, * ut déstruas inimícum et ultórem.

content.latin: 8:4 Quóniam vidébo cælos tuos, ópera digitórum tuórum: * lunam et stellas, quæ tu fundásti.
content.english: 8:4 For I will behold thy heavens, the works of thy fingers: * the moon and the stars which thou hast founded.

segments.t: Quóniam vidébo cælos tuos, ópera digitórum tuórum: * lunam et stellas, quæ tu fundásti.

content.latin: 8:5 Quid est homo quod memor es eius? * aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum?
content.english: 8:5 What is man that thou art mindful of him? * or the son of man that thou visitest him?

segments.t: Quid est homo quod memor es eius? * aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum?

content.latin: 8:6 Minuísti eum paulo minus ab Ángelis, glória et honóre coronásti eum: * et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
content.english: 8:6 Thou hast made him a little less than the angels, thou hast crowned him with glory and honour: * and hast set him over the works of thy hands.

segments.t: Minuísti eum paulo minus ab Ángelis, glória et honóre coronásti eum: * et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.

content.latin: 8:8 Ómnia subiecísti sub pédibus eius, * oves et boves univérsas: ínsuper et pécora campi.
content.english: 8:8 Thou hast subjected all things under his feet, * all sheep and oxen: moreover the beasts also of the fields.

segments.t: Ómnia subiecísti sub pédibus eius, * oves et boves univérsas: ínsuper et pécora campi.

content.latin: 8:9 Vólucres cæli, et pisces maris, * qui perámbulant sémitas maris.
content.english: 8:9 The birds of the air, and the fishes of the sea, * that pass through the paths of the sea.

segments.t: Vólucres cæli, et pisces maris, * qui perámbulant sémitas maris.

content.latin: 8:10 Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
content.english: 8:10 O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in all the earth!

segments.t: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!

content.english: Ant. The Lord discovered the thickets, * and in His temple every whit of it uttereth His glory.

segments.t: Ant.
Revelávit Dóminus * condénsa, et in templo eius omnes dicent glóriam.

content.latin: Psalmus 28 [2]
content.english: Psalm 28 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 28

content.latin: 28:1 Afférte Dómino, fílii Dei: * afférte Dómino fílios aríetum.
content.english: 28:1 Bring to the Lord, O ye children of God: * bring to the Lord the offspring of rams.

segments.t: Afférte Dómino, fílii Dei: * afférte Dómino fílios aríetum.

content.latin: 28:2 Afférte Dómino glóriam et honórem, afférte Dómino glóriam nómini eius: * adoráte Dóminum in átrio sancto eius.
content.english: 28:2 Bring to the Lord glory and honour: bring to the Lord glory to his name: * adore ye the Lord in his holy court.

segments.t: Afférte Dómino glóriam et honórem, afférte Dómino glóriam nómini eius: * adoráte Dóminum in átrio sancto eius.

content.latin: 28:3 Vox Dómini super aquas, Deus maiestátis intónuit: * Dóminus super aquas multas.
content.english: 28:3 The voice of the Lord is upon the waters; the God of majesty hath thundered, * The Lord is upon many waters.

segments.t: Vox Dómini super aquas, Deus maiestátis intónuit: * Dóminus super aquas multas.

content.latin: 28:4 Vox Dómini in virtúte: * vox Dómini in magnificéntia.
content.english: 28:4 The voice of the Lord is in power; * the voice of the Lord in magnificence.

segments.t: Vox Dómini in virtúte: * vox Dómini in magnificéntia.

content.latin: 28:5 Vox Dómini confringéntis cedros: * et confrínget Dóminus cedros Líbani:
content.english: 28:5 The voice of the Lord breaketh the cedars: * yea, the Lord shall break the cedars of Libanus.

segments.t: Vox Dómini confringéntis cedros: * et confrínget Dóminus cedros Líbani:

content.latin: 28:6 Et commínuet eas tamquam vítulum Líbani: * et diléctus quemádmodum fílius unicórnium.
content.english: 28:6 And shall reduce them to pieces, as a calf of Libanus, * and as the beloved son of unicorns.

segments.t: Et commínuet eas tamquam vítulum Líbani: * et diléctus quemádmodum fílius unicórnium.

content.latin: 28:7 Vox Dómini intercidéntis flammam ignis: * vox Dómini concutiéntis desértum: et commovébit Dóminus desértum Cades.
content.english: 28:7 The voice of the Lord divideth the flame of fire: * The voice of the Lord shaketh the desert: and the Lord shall shake the desert of Cades.

segments.t: Vox Dómini intercidéntis flammam ignis: * vox Dómini concutiéntis desértum: et commovébit Dóminus desértum Cades.

content.latin: 28:9 Vox Dómini præparántis cervos, et revelábit condénsa: * et in templo eius omnes dicent glóriam.
content.english: 28:9 The voice of the Lord prepareth the stags: and he will discover the thick woods: * and in his temple all shall speak his glory.

segments.t: Vox Dómini præparántis cervos, et revelábit condénsa: * et in templo eius omnes dicent glóriam.

content.latin: 28:10 Dóminus dilúvium inhabitáre facit: * et sedébit Dóminus Rex in ætérnum.
content.english: 28:10 The Lord maketh the flood to dwell: * and the Lord shall sit king for ever.

segments.t: Dóminus dilúvium inhabitáre facit: * et sedébit Dóminus Rex in ætérnum.

content.latin: 28:11 Dóminus virtútem pópulo suo dabit: * Dóminus benedícet pópulo suo in pace.
content.english: 28:11 The Lord will give strength to his people: * the Lord will bless his people with peace.

segments.t: Dóminus virtútem pópulo suo dabit: * Dóminus benedícet pópulo suo in pace.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Ant. Speciósus forma * præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis.
content.english: Ant. Thou art fairer than the children of men * grace is poured into thy lips.

segments.t: Ant.
Speciósus forma * præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis.

content.latin: Psalmus 44 [3]
content.english: Psalm 44 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 44

content.latin: 44:2 Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.
content.english: 44:2 My heart hath uttered a good word; * I speak my works to the King.

segments.t: Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.

content.latin: 44:2 Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.
content.english: 44:2 My tongue is the pen of a scrivener * that writeth swiftly.

segments.t: Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.

content.latin: 44:3 Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
content.english: 44:3 Thou art beautiful above the sons of men: grace is poured abroad in thy lips; * therefore hath God blessed thee for ever.

segments.t: Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.

content.latin: 44:4 Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.
content.english: 44:4 Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, * O thou most mighty.

segments.t: Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.

content.latin: 44:5 Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
content.english: 44:5 With thy comeliness and thy beauty * set out, proceed prosperously, and reign.

segments.t: Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.

content.latin: 44:5 Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
content.english: 44:5 Because of truth and meekness and justice: * and thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.

segments.t: Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.

content.latin: 44:6 Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.
content.english: 44:6 Thy arrows are sharp: under thee shall people fall, * into the hearts of the king’s enemies.

segments.t: Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.

content.latin: 44:7 Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.
content.english: 44:7 Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: * the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness.

segments.t: Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.

content.latin: 44:8 Dilexísti iustítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.
content.english: 44:8 Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity: * therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.

segments.t: Dilexísti iustítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.

content.latin: 44:9 Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.
content.english: 44:9 Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume thy garments, from the ivory houses: * out of which the daughters of kings have delighted thee in thy glory.

segments.t: Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.

content.latin: 44:10 Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.
content.english: 44:10 The queen stood on thy right hand, in gilded clothing; * surrounded with variety.

segments.t: Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.

content.latin: 44:11 Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.
content.english: 44:11 Hearken, O daughter, and see, and incline thy ear: * and forget thy people and thy father’s house.

segments.t: Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.

content.latin: 44:12 Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.
content.english: 44:12 And the king shall greatly desire thy beauty; * for he is the Lord thy God, and him they shall adore.

segments.t: Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.

content.latin: 44:13 Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.
content.english: 44:13 And the daughters of Tyre with gifts, * yea, all the rich among the people, shall entreat thy countenance.

segments.t: Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.

content.latin: 44:14 Omnis glória eius fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis circumamícta varietátibus.
content.english: 44:14 All the glory of the king’s daughter is within, * in golden borders, clothed round about with varieties.

segments.t: Omnis glória eius fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis circumamícta varietátibus.

content.latin: 44:15 Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ eius afferéntur tibi.
content.english: 44:15 After her shall virgins be brought to the king: * her neighbours shall be brought to thee.

segments.t: Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ eius afferéntur tibi.

content.latin: 44:16 Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.
content.english: 44:16 They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing: * they shall be brought into the temple of the king.

segments.t: Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.

content.latin: 44:17 Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.
content.english: 44:17 Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee: * thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.

segments.t: Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.

content.latin: 44:18 Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
content.english: 44:18 They shall remember thy name * throughout all generations.

segments.t: Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.

content.latin: 44:18 Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 44:18 Therefore shall people praise thee for ever; yea, * for ever and ever.

segments.t: Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis.
content.english: Ant. Thou art fairer than the children of men grace is poured into thy lips.

segments.t: Ant.
Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis.

content.latin: ℣. Gloriósus apparuísti in conspéctu Dómini.
content.english: ℣. Thou wast manifested in thy glory in the Presence of the Lord.

segments.t: Gloriósus apparuísti in conspéctu Dómini.

content.latin: ℟. Proptérea decórem índuit te Dóminus.
content.english: ℟. Therefore the Lord hath clothed thee with majesty.

segments.t: Proptérea decórem índuit te Dóminus.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

segments.t: Absolutio.
Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.english: Lesson from the second letter of St. Peter the Apostle

content.latin: 10 Fratres: Magis satágite, ut per bona ópera certam vestram vocatiónem et electiónem faciátis: hæc enim faciéntes, non peccábitis aliquándo.
content.english: 10 Wherefore, brethren, labour the more, that by good works you may make sure your calling and election. For doing these things, you shall not sin at any time.

segments.t: Fratres: Magis satágite, ut per bona ópera certam vestram vocatiónem et electiónem faciátis: hæc enim faciéntes, non peccábitis aliquándo.

content.latin: 11 Sic enim abundánter ministrábitur vobis intróitus in ætérnum regnum Dómini nostri, et Salvatóris Iesu Christi.
content.english: 11 For so an entrance shall be ministered to you abundantly into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.

segments.t: Sic enim abundánter ministrábitur vobis intróitus in ætérnum regnum Dómini nostri, et Salvatóris Iesu Christi.

content.latin: 12 Propter quod incípiam vos semper commonére de his: et quidem sciéntes et confirmátos vos in præsénti veritáte.
content.english: 12 For which cause I will begin to put you always in remembrance of these things: though indeed you know them, and are confirmed in the present truth.

segments.t: Propter quod incípiam vos semper commonére de his: et quidem sciéntes et confirmátos vos in præsénti veritáte.

content.latin: 13 Iustum autem árbitror, quámdiu sum in hoc tabernáculo, suscitáre vos in commonitióne:
content.english: 13 But I think it meet as long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir you up by putting you in remembrance.

segments.t: Iustum autem árbitror, quámdiu sum in hoc tabernáculo, suscitáre vos in commonitióne:

content.latin: 14 Certus quod velox est deposítio tabernáculi mei secúndum quod et Dóminus noster Iesus Christus significávit mihi.
content.english: 14 Being assured that the laying away of this my tabernacle is at hand, according as our Lord Jesus Christ also hath signified to me.

segments.t: Certus quod velox est deposítio tabernáculi mei secúndum quod et Dóminus noster Iesus Christus significávit mihi.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Surge, illumináre, Ierúsalem, quia venit lumen tuum,
content.english: ℟. Arise, shine, O Jerusalem, for thy light is come:

segments.t: Surge, illumináre, Ierúsalem, quia venit lumen tuum,

content.latin: * Et glória Dómini super te orta est.
content.english: * And the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.

content.latin: ℣. Et ambulábunt gentes in lúmine tuo, et reges in splendóre ortus tui.
content.english: ℣. And the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising.

segments.t: Et ambulábunt gentes in lúmine tuo, et reges in splendóre ortus tui.

content.latin: ℟. Et glória Dómini super te orta est.
content.english: ℟. And the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.

segments.t: Et glória Dómini super te orta est.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.
content.english: Benediction. May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 15 Dabo autem óperam et frequénter habére vos post óbitum meum, ut horum memóriam faciátis.
content.english: 15 And I will endeavour, that you frequently have after my decease, whereby you may keep a memory of these things.

segments.t: Dabo autem óperam et frequénter habére vos post óbitum meum, ut horum memóriam faciátis.

content.latin: 16 Non enim doctas fábulas secúti notam fécimus vobis Dómini nostri Iesu Christi virtútem et præséntiam, sed speculatóres facti illíus magnitúdinis.
content.english: 16 For we have not by following artificial fables, made known to you the power, and presence of our Lord Jesus Christ; but we were eyewitnesses of his greatness.

segments.t: Non enim doctas fábulas secúti notam fécimus vobis Dómini nostri Iesu Christi virtútem et præséntiam, sed speculatóres facti illíus magnitúdinis.

content.latin: 17 Accípiens enim a Deo Patre honórem et glóriam, voce delápsa ad eum huiuscémodi a magnífica glória: Hic est Fílius meus diléctus, in quo mihi complácui; ipsum audíte.
content.english: 17 For he received from God the Father, honour and glory: this voice coming down to him from the excellent glory: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.

segments.t: Accípiens enim a Deo Patre honórem et glóriam, voce delápsa ad eum huiuscémodi a magnífica glória: Hic est Fílius meus diléctus, in quo mihi complácui; ipsum audíte.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. In splendénte nube Spíritus Sanctus visus est, Patérna vox audíta est:
content.english: ℟. The Holy Ghost was manifested in the bright cloud and the Father was heard:

segments.t: In splendénte nube Spíritus Sanctus visus est, Patérna vox audíta est:

content.latin: * Hic est Fílius meus diléctus, in quo mihi bene complácui; ipsum audíte.
content.english: * This is My beloved Son, in Whom I am well pleased; hear ye Him.

content.latin: ℣. Appáruit nubes obúmbrans, et vox Patris intónuit.
content.english: ℣. There was a cloud that overshadowed them, and the voice of the Father came out thereof in thunder.

segments.t: Appáruit nubes obúmbrans, et vox Patris intónuit.

content.latin: ℟. Hic est Fílius meus diléctus, in quo mihi bene complácui; ipsum audíte.
content.english: ℟. This is My beloved Son, in Whom I am well pleased; hear ye Him.

segments.t: Hic est Fílius meus diléctus, in quo mihi bene complácui; ipsum audíte.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.
content.english: Benediction. May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 18 Et hanc vocem nos audívimus de cælo allátam, cum essémus cum ipso in monte sancto.
content.english: 18 And this voice we heard brought from heaven, when we were with him in the holy mount.

segments.t: Et hanc vocem nos audívimus de cælo allátam, cum essémus cum ipso in monte sancto.

content.latin: 19 Et habémus firmiórem prophéticum sermónem, cui bene fácitis attendéntes quasi lucérnæ lucénti in caliginóso loco, donec dies elucéscat et lúcifer oriátur in córdibus vestris,
content.english: 19 And we have the more firm prophetical word: whereunto you do well to attend, as to a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts:

segments.t: Et habémus firmiórem prophéticum sermónem, cui bene fácitis attendéntes quasi lucérnæ lucénti in caliginóso loco, donec dies elucéscat et lúcifer oriátur in córdibus vestris,

content.latin: 20 Hoc primum intellegéntes quod omnis prophetía Scriptúræ própria interpretatióne non fit.
content.english: 20 Understanding this first, that no prophecy of scripture is made by private interpretation.

segments.t: Hoc primum intellegéntes quod omnis prophetía Scriptúræ própria interpretatióne non fit.

content.latin: 21 Non enim voluntáte humána alláta est aliquándo prophetía; sed Spíritu Sancto inspiráti locúti sunt sancti Dei hómines.
content.english: 21 For prophecy came not by the will of man at any time: but the holy men of God spoke, inspired by the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Non enim voluntáte humána alláta est aliquándo prophetía; sed Spíritu Sancto inspiráti locúti sunt sancti Dei hómines.

content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.english: ℟. Behold what manner of love God the Father hath bestowed upon us,

segments.t: Vidéte qualem caritátem dedit nobis Deus Pater,

content.english: ℣. We know that when He shall appear, we shall be like Him, for we shall see Him as He is.

segments.t: Scimus quóniam, cum apparúerit, símiles ei érimus, quóniam vidébimus eum sícuti est.

content.latin: Ant. Illúminans * tu mirabíliter a móntibus ætérnis: turbáti sunt omnes insipiéntes corde.
content.english: Ant. When Thou didst make thy light to shine forth right wondrously * from the everlasting hills, all they that were foolish of heart were troubled.

segments.t: Ant.
Illúminans * tu mirabíliter a móntibus ætérnis: turbáti sunt omnes insipiéntes corde.

content.latin: Psalmus 75 [4]
content.english: Psalm 75 [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 75

content.latin: 75:2 Notus in Iudǽa Deus: * in Israël magnum nomen eius.
content.english: 75:2 In Judea God is known: * his name is great in Israel.

segments.t: Notus in Iudǽa Deus: * in Israël magnum nomen eius.

content.latin: 75:3 Et factus est in pace locus eius: * et habitátio eius in Sion.
content.english: 75:3 And his place is in peace: * and his abode in Sion:

segments.t: Et factus est in pace locus eius: * et habitátio eius in Sion.

content.latin: 75:4 Ibi confrégit poténtias árcuum, * scutum, gládium, et bellum.
content.english: 75:4 There hath he broken the powers of bows, * the shield, the sword, and the battle.

segments.t: Ibi confrégit poténtias árcuum, * scutum, gládium, et bellum.

content.latin: 75:5 Illúminans tu mirabíliter a móntibus ætérnis: * turbáti sunt omnes insipiéntes corde.
content.english: 75:5 Thou enlightenest wonderfully from the everlasting hills. * All the foolish of heart were troubled.

segments.t: Illúminans tu mirabíliter a móntibus ætérnis: * turbáti sunt omnes insipiéntes corde.

content.latin: 75:6 Dormiérunt somnum suum: * et nihil invenérunt omnes viri divitiárum in mánibus suis.
content.english: 75:6 They have slept their sleep; * and all the men of riches have found nothing in their hands.

segments.t: Dormiérunt somnum suum: * et nihil invenérunt omnes viri divitiárum in mánibus suis.

content.latin: 75:7 Ab increpatióne tua, Deus Iacob, * dormitavérunt qui ascendérunt equos.
content.english: 75:7 At thy rebuke, O God of Jacob, * they have all slumbered that mounted on horseback.

segments.t: Ab increpatióne tua, Deus Iacob, * dormitavérunt qui ascendérunt equos.

content.latin: 75:8 Tu terríbilis es, et quis resístet tibi? * ex tunc ira tua.
content.english: 75:8 Thou art terrible, and who shall resist thee? * from that time thy wrath.

segments.t: Tu terríbilis es, et quis resístet tibi? * ex tunc ira tua.

content.latin: 75:9 De cælo audítum fecísti iudícium: * terra trémuit et quiévit,
content.english: 75:9 Thou hast caused judgment to be heard from heaven: * the earth trembled and was still,

segments.t: De cælo audítum fecísti iudícium: * terra trémuit et quiévit,

content.latin: 75:10 Cum exsúrgeret in iudícium Deus, * ut salvos fáceret omnes mansuétos terræ.
content.english: 75:10 When God arose in judgment, * to save all the meek of the earth.

segments.t: Cum exsúrgeret in iudícium Deus, * ut salvos fáceret omnes mansuétos terræ.

content.latin: 75:11 Quóniam cogitátio hóminis confitébitur tibi: * et relíquiæ cogitatiónis diem festum agent tibi.
content.english: 75:11 For the thought of man shall give praise to thee: * and the remainders of the thought shall keep holiday to thee.

segments.t: Quóniam cogitátio hóminis confitébitur tibi: * et relíquiæ cogitatiónis diem festum agent tibi.

content.latin: 75:12 Vovéte, et réddite Dómino, Deo vestro: * omnes, qui in circúitu eius affértis múnera.
content.english: 75:12 Vow ye, and pay to the Lord your God: * all you that are round about him bring presents.

segments.t: Vovéte, et réddite Dómino, Deo vestro: * omnes, qui in circúitu eius affértis múnera.

content.latin: 75:13 Terríbili et ei qui aufert spíritum príncipum, * terríbili apud reges terræ.
content.english: 75:13 To him that is terrible, even to him who taketh away the spirit of princes: * to the terrible with the kings of the earth.

segments.t: Terríbili et ei qui aufert spíritum príncipum, * terríbili apud reges terræ.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Illúminans tu mirabíliter a móntibus ætérnis: turbáti sunt omnes insipiéntes corde.
content.english: Ant. When Thou didst make thy light to shine forth right wondrously from the everlasting hills, all they that were foolish of heart were troubled.

segments.t: Ant.
Illúminans tu mirabíliter a móntibus ætérnis: turbáti sunt omnes insipiéntes corde.

content.english: Ant. A day in thy courts * is better than a thousand.

segments.t: Ant.
Mélior est * dies una in átriis tuis, super míllia.

content.latin: Psalmus 83 [5]
content.english: Psalm 83 [5]

segments.t: Psalmus 83

content.latin: 83:2 Quam dilécta tabernácula tua, Dómine virtútum: * concupíscit, et déficit ánima mea in átria Dómini.
content.english: 83:2 How lovely are thy tabernacles, O Lord of hosts! * my soul longeth and fainteth for the courts of the Lord.

segments.t: Quam dilécta tabernácula tua, Dómine virtútum: * concupíscit, et déficit ánima mea in átria Dómini.

content.latin: 83:3 Cor meum, et caro mea * exsultavérunt in Deum vivum.
content.english: 83:3 My heart and my flesh * have rejoiced in the living God.

segments.t: Cor meum, et caro mea * exsultavérunt in Deum vivum.

content.latin: 83:4 Étenim passer invénit sibi domum: * et turtur nidum sibi, ubi ponat pullos suos.
content.english: 83:4 For the sparrow hath found herself a house, * and the turtledove a nest for herself where she may lay her young ones:

segments.t: Étenim passer invénit sibi domum: * et turtur nidum sibi, ubi ponat pullos suos.

content.latin: 83:4 Altária tua, Dómine virtútum: * Rex meus, et Deus meus.
content.english: 83:4 Thy altars, O Lord of hosts, * my king and my God.

segments.t: Altária tua, Dómine virtútum: * Rex meus, et Deus meus.

content.latin: 83:5 Beáti, qui hábitant in domo tua, Dómine: * in sǽcula sæculórum laudábunt te.
content.english: 83:5 Blessed are they that dwell in thy house, O Lord: * they shall praise thee for ever and ever.

segments.t: Beáti, qui hábitant in domo tua, Dómine: * in sǽcula sæculórum laudábunt te.

content.latin: 83:6 Beátus vir, cuius est auxílium abs te: * ascensiónes in corde suo dispósuit, in valle lacrimárum in loco, quem pósuit.
content.english: 83:6 Blessed is the man whose help is from thee: * in his heart he hath disposed to ascend by steps, in the vale of tears, in the place which he hath set.

segments.t: Beátus vir, cuius est auxílium abs te: * ascensiónes in corde suo dispósuit, in valle lacrimárum in loco, quem pósuit.

content.latin: 83:8 Étenim benedictiónem dabit legislátor, ibunt de virtúte in virtútem: * vidébitur Deus deórum in Sion.

content.latin: Aperit Dóminus coram eléctis téstibus glóriam suam, et commúnem illam cum céteris córporis formam tanto splendóre claríficat, ut et fácies eius solis fulgóri símilis, et vestítus candóri nívium esset æquális. In qua transfiguratióne illud quidem principáliter agebátur, ut de córdibus discipulórum crucis scándalum tollerétur; nec conturbáret eórum fidem voluntáriæ humílitas passiónis, quibus reveláta esset abscónditæ excelléntia dignitátis. Sed non minóre providéntia spes sanctæ Ecclésiæ fundabátur, ut totum Christi corpus agnósceret quali esset commutatióne donándum, ut eius sibi honóris consórtium membra promítterent, qui in cápite præfulsísset.
content.english: The Lord taketh chosen witnesses, and in their presence, revealeth His glory. That form of body which He had in common with other men, He so transfigured with light, that His Face did shine as the sun, and His raiment became exceeding white as snow. Of this metamorphosis the chief work was to remove from the hearts of the disciples the stumbling at the Cross. Before their eyes was unveiled the splendour of His hidden majesty, that the lowliness of His freely-chosen suffering might not confound their faith. But none the less was there here laid by the Providence of God a solid foundation for the hope of the Holy Church, whereby the whole body of Christ should know with what a change it is yet to be honoured. The members of that body whose Head hath already been transfigured in light may promise themselves a share in His glory.

content.latin: Confirmándis vero Apóstolis et ad omnem sciéntiam provehéndis, ália quoque in illo miráculo accéssit instrúctio. Móyses enim et Elías, lex scílicet et prophétæ apparuérunt cum Dómino loquéntes; ut veríssime in illa quinque virórum præséntia complerétur quod dictum est: in duóbus vel tribus téstibus stat omne verbum. Quid hoc stabílius, quid fírmius verbo, in cuius prædicatióne véteris et novi Testaménti cóncinit tuba, et cum evangélica doctrína, antiquárum protestatiónum instruménta concúrrunt? Astipulántur enim sibi ínvicem utriúsque Fœ́deris páginæ; et, quem sub velámine mysteriórum præcedéntia signa promíserant, maniféstum atque perspícuum præséntis glóriæ splendor osténdit.
content.english: For the strengthening the Apostles and bringing them forward into all knowledge, there appeared unto them Moses and Elias that is, the Law and the Prophets talking with Him. Before five witnesses did His glorification take place, as though to fulfill that which is written: At the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established. Deut. xix. 15. What can be more certain, what can be better attested than this matter, which is proclaimed by the trumpets of both the Old and the New Testaments, and concerning which the witness of ancient testimony uniteth with the teaching of the Gospel? The pages of either Covenant strengthen one another, and the brightness of open glory maketh manifest and distinct Him Whom the former prophecies had promised under the veil of mysteries.

content.latin: His ergo sacramentórum revelatiónibus Petrus Apóstolus incitátus, mundána spernens et terréna fastídiens, in æternórum desidérium quodam mentis rapiebátur excéssu; et, gáudio totíus visiónis implétus, ibi cum Iesu optábat habitáre, ubi manifésta eius glória lætabátur. Unde et ait: Dómine, bonum est nos hic esse: si vis, faciámus hic tria tabernácula; tibi unum, Móysi unum et Elíæ unum. Sed huic suggestióni Dóminus non respóndit, signíficans, non quidem ímprobum, sed inordinátum esse quod cúperet; cum salvári mundus, nisi Christi morte, non posset, et exémplo Dómini in hoc vocarétur credéntium fides, ut licet non oportéret de beatitúdinis promissiónibus dubitári, intellegerémus tamen inter tentatiónes huius vitæ prius nobis tolerántiam postulándam esse, quam glóriam.
content.english: The unveiling of such mysteries roused the mind of the Apostle Peter to an outburst of longing for the things eternal, which despised and disdained the things worldly and earthly overflowing with gladness at the vision, he yearned to dwell with Jesus there, where the revelation of His glory had rejoiced him. And so he said Master, it is good for us to be here if Thou wilt, let us make here three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias. To this proposal the Lord answered nothing, this signifying, that what Peter wished was not wrong, but out of place, since the world could not be saved but by the death of Christ. And the Lord's example was to call the faith of believers to this, that albeit we are behoven to have no doubts concerning the promise of eternal blessedness, yet we are to understand that, amid the trials of this life, we are to seek for endurance before glory.

segments.t: Tui sunt cæli, et tua est terra, orbem terræ et plenitúdinem eius tu fundásti: * aquilónem, et mare tu creásti.

content.latin: 88:13 Thabor et Hermon in nómine tuo exsultábunt: * tuum brácchium cum poténtia.
content.english: 88:13 Thabor and Hermon shall rejoice in thy name: * thy arm is with might.

segments.t: Thabor et Hermon in nómine tuo exsultábunt: * tuum brácchium cum poténtia.

content.latin: 88:14 Firmétur manus tua, et exaltétur déxtera tua: * iustítia et iudícium præparátio sedis tuæ.
content.english: 88:14 Let thy hand be strengthened, and thy right hand exalted: * justice and judgment are the preparation of thy throne.

segments.t: Firmétur manus tua, et exaltétur déxtera tua: * iustítia et iudícium præparátio sedis tuæ.

content.latin: 88:15 Misericórdia et véritas præcédent fáciem tuam: * beátus pópulus, qui scit iubilatiónem.
content.english: 88:15 Mercy and truth shall go before thy face: * blessed is the people that knoweth jubilation.

segments.t: Misericórdia et véritas præcédent fáciem tuam: * beátus pópulus, qui scit iubilatiónem.

content.latin: 88:16 Dómine, in lúmine vultus tui ambulábunt, et in nómine tuo exsultábunt tota die: * et in iustítia tua exaltabúntur.
content.english: 88:16 They shall walk, O Lord, in the light of thy countenance: and in thy name they shall rejoice all the day, * and in thy justice they shall be exalted.

segments.t: Dómine, in lúmine vultus tui ambulábunt, et in nómine tuo exsultábunt tota die: * et in iustítia tua exaltabúntur.

content.latin: 88:18 Quóniam glória virtútis eórum tu es: * et in beneplácito tuo exaltábitur cornu nostrum.
content.english: 88:18 For thou art the glory of their strength: * and in thy good pleasure shall our horn be exalted.

segments.t: Quóniam glória virtútis eórum tu es: * et in beneplácito tuo exaltábitur cornu nostrum.

content.latin: 88:19 Quia Dómini est assúmptio nostra, * et Sancti Israël, regis nostri.
content.english: 88:19 For our protection is of the Lord, * and of our king the holy one of Israel.

segments.t: Quia Dómini est assúmptio nostra, * et Sancti Israël, regis nostri.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Thabor et Hermon in nómine tuo exsultábunt: tuum brácchium cum poténtia.
content.english: Ant. Tabor and Hermon shall rejoice in thy Name. Thou hast a mighty arm.

segments.t: Ant.
Thabor et Hermon in nómine tuo exsultábunt: tuum brácchium cum poténtia.

content.latin: Ant. Lux orta est * iusto, et rectis corde lætítia.
content.english: Ant. Light is sprung up for the righteous, * and gladness for the upright in heart.

segments.t: Ant.
Lux orta est * iusto, et rectis corde lætítia.

content.latin: Psalmus 96 [8]
content.english: Psalm 96 [8]

segments.t: Psalmus 96

content.latin: 96:1 Dóminus regnávit, exsúltet terra: * læténtur ínsulæ multæ.
content.english: 96:1 The Lord hath reigned, let the earth rejoice: * let many islands be glad.

segments.t: Dóminus regnávit, exsúltet terra: * læténtur ínsulæ multæ.

content.latin: 96:2 Nubes, et calígo in circúitu eius: * iustítia, et iudícium corréctio sedis eius.
content.english: 96:2 Clouds and darkness are round about him: * justice and judgment are the establishment of his throne.

segments.t: Nubes, et calígo in circúitu eius: * iustítia, et iudícium corréctio sedis eius.

content.latin: 96:3 Ignis ante ipsum præcédet, * et inflammábit in circúitu inimícos eius.
content.english: 96:3 A fire shall go before him, * and shall burn his enemies round about.

segments.t: Ignis ante ipsum præcédet, * et inflammábit in circúitu inimícos eius.

content.latin: 96:4 Illuxérunt fúlgura eius orbi terræ: * vidit, et commóta est terra.
content.english: 96:4 His lightnings have shone forth to the world: * the earth saw and trembled.

segments.t: Illuxérunt fúlgura eius orbi terræ: * vidit, et commóta est terra.

content.latin: 96:5 Montes, sicut cera fluxérunt a fácie Dómini: * a fácie Dómini omnis terra.
content.english: 96:5 The mountains melted like wax, at the presence of the Lord: * at the presence of the Lord of all the earth.

segments.t: Montes, sicut cera fluxérunt a fácie Dómini: * a fácie Dómini omnis terra.

content.latin: 96:6 Annuntiavérunt cæli iustítiam eius: * et vidérunt omnes pópuli glóriam eius.
content.english: 96:6 The heavens declared his justice: * and all people saw his glory.

segments.t: Annuntiavérunt cæli iustítiam eius: * et vidérunt omnes pópuli glóriam eius.

content.latin: 96:7 Confundántur omnes, qui adórant sculptília: * et qui gloriántur in simulácris suis.
content.english: 96:7 Let them be all confounded that adore graven things, * and that glory in their idols.

segments.t: Confundántur omnes, qui adórant sculptília: * et qui gloriántur in simulácris suis.

content.latin: 96:7 Adoráte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * audívit, et lætáta est Sion.
content.english: 96:7 Adore him, all you his angels: * Sion heard, and was glad.

segments.t: Adoráte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * audívit, et lætáta est Sion.

content.latin: 96:8 Et exsultavérunt fíliæ Iudæ, * propter iudícia tua, Dómine:
content.english: 96:8 And the daughters of Juda rejoiced, * because of thy judgments, O Lord.

segments.t: Et exsultavérunt fíliæ Iudæ, * propter iudícia tua, Dómine:

content.latin: 96:9 Quóniam tu Dóminus Altíssimus super omnem terram: * nimis exaltátus es super omnes deos.
content.english: 96:9 For thou art the most high Lord over all the earth: * thou art exalted exceedingly above all gods.

segments.t: Quóniam tu Dóminus Altíssimus super omnem terram: * nimis exaltátus es super omnes deos.

content.latin: 96:10 Qui dilígitis Dóminum, odíte malum: * custódit Dóminus ánimas sanctórum suórum, de manu peccatóris liberábit eos.
content.english: 96:10 You that love the Lord, hate evil: * the Lord preserveth the souls of his saints, he will deliver them out of the hand of the sinner.

segments.t: Qui dilígitis Dóminum, odíte malum: * custódit Dóminus ánimas sanctórum suórum, de manu peccatóris liberábit eos.

content.latin: 96:11 Lux orta est iusto, * et rectis corde lætítia.
content.english: 96:11 Light is risen to the just, * and joy to the right of heart.

segments.t: Lux orta est iusto, * et rectis corde lætítia.

content.latin: 96:12 Lætámini, iusti, in Dómino: * et confitémini memóriæ sanctificatiónis eius.
content.english: 96:12 Rejoice, ye just, in the Lord: * and give praise to the remembrance of his holiness.

segments.t: Lætámini, iusti, in Dómino: * et confitémini memóriæ sanctificatiónis eius.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Lux orta est iusto, et rectis corde lætítia.
content.english: Ant. Light is sprung up for the righteous, and gladness for the upright in heart.

segments.t: Ant.
Lux orta est iusto, et rectis corde lætítia.

content.latin: Ant. Confessiónem * et decórem índuit, amíctus lúmine sicut vestiménto.
content.english: Ant. He was clothed with honour and majesty, * covering Himself with light as with a garment.

segments.t: Ant.
Confessiónem * et decórem índuit, amíctus lúmine sicut vestiménto.

content.latin: Psalmus 103 [9]
content.english: Psalm 103 [9]

segments.t: Psalmus 103

content.latin: 103:1 Bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino: * Dómine, Deus meus, magnificátus es veheménter.
content.english: 103:1 Bless the Lord, O my soul: * O Lord my God, thou art exceedingly great.

segments.t: Bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino: * Dómine, Deus meus, magnificátus es veheménter.

content.latin: 103:1 Confessiónem, et decórem induísti: * amíctus lúmine sicut vestiménto:
content.english: 103:1 Thou hast put on praise and beauty: * and art clothed with light as with a garment.

segments.t: Confessiónem, et decórem induísti: * amíctus lúmine sicut vestiménto:

content.latin: 103:2 Exténdens cælum sicut pellem: * qui tegis aquis superióra eius.
content.english: 103:2 Who stretchest out the heaven like a pavilion: * who coverest the higher rooms thereof with water.

segments.t: Exténdens cælum sicut pellem: * qui tegis aquis superióra eius.

content.latin: 103:3 Qui ponis nubem ascénsum tuum: * qui ámbulas super pennas ventórum.
content.english: 103:3 Who makest the clouds thy chariot: * who walkest upon the wings of the winds.

segments.t: Qui ponis nubem ascénsum tuum: * qui ámbulas super pennas ventórum.

content.latin: 103:4 Qui facis ángelos tuos, spíritus: * et minístros tuos ignem uréntem.
content.english: 103:4 Who makest thy angels spirits: * and thy ministers a burning fire.

segments.t: Qui facis ángelos tuos, spíritus: * et minístros tuos ignem uréntem.

content.latin: 103:5 Qui fundásti terram super stabilitátem suam: * non inclinábitur in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 103:5 Who hast founded the earth upon its own bases: * it shall not be moved for ever and ever.

segments.t: Qui fundásti terram super stabilitátem suam: * non inclinábitur in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: 103:6 Abýssus, sicut vestiméntum, amíctus eius: * super montes stabunt aquæ.
content.english: 103:6 The deep like a garment is its clothing: * above the mountains shall the waters stand.

segments.t: Abýssus, sicut vestiméntum, amíctus eius: * super montes stabunt aquæ.

content.latin: 103:7 Ab increpatióne tua fúgient: * a voce tonítrui tui formidábunt.
content.english: 103:7 At thy rebuke they shall flee: * at the voice of thy thunder they shall fear.

segments.t: Ab increpatióne tua fúgient: * a voce tonítrui tui formidábunt.

content.latin: 103:8 Ascéndunt montes: et descéndunt campi * in locum, quem fundásti eis.
content.english: 103:8 The mountains ascend, and the plains descend * into the place which thou hast founded for them.

segments.t: Ascéndunt montes: et descéndunt campi * in locum, quem fundásti eis.

content.latin: 103:9 Términum posuísti, quem non transgrediéntur: * neque converténtur operíre terram.
content.english: 103:9 Thou hast set a bound which they shall not pass over; * neither shall they return to cover the earth.

segments.t: Términum posuísti, quem non transgrediéntur: * neque converténtur operíre terram.

content.latin: 103:10 Qui emíttis fontes in convállibus: * inter médium móntium pertransíbunt aquæ.
content.english: 103:10 Thou sendest forth springs in the vales: * between the midst of the hills the waters shall pass.

segments.t: Qui emíttis fontes in convállibus: * inter médium móntium pertransíbunt aquæ.

content.latin: 103:11 Potábunt omnes béstiæ agri: * exspectábunt ónagri in siti sua.
content.english: 103:11 All the beasts of the field shall drink: * the wild asses shall expect in their thirst.

segments.t: Potábunt omnes béstiæ agri: * exspectábunt ónagri in siti sua.

content.latin: 103:12 Super ea vólucres cæli habitábunt: * de médio petrárum dabunt voces.
content.english: 103:12 Over them the birds of the air shall dwell: * from the midst of the rocks they shall give forth their voices.

segments.t: Super ea vólucres cæli habitábunt: * de médio petrárum dabunt voces.

content.latin: 103:13 Rigans montes de superióribus suis: * de fructu óperum tuórum satiábitur terra:
content.english: 103:13 Thou waterest the hills from thy upper rooms: * the earth shall be filled with the fruit of thy works:

segments.t: Rigans montes de superióribus suis: * de fructu óperum tuórum satiábitur terra:

content.latin: 103:14 Prodúcens fænum iuméntis, * et herbam servitúti hóminum:
content.english: 103:14 Bringing forth grass for cattle, * and herb for the service of men.

segments.t: Prodúcens fænum iuméntis, * et herbam servitúti hóminum:

content.latin: 103:14 Ut edúcas panem de terra: * et vinum lætíficet cor hóminis:
content.english: 103:14 That thou mayst bring bread out of the earth: * and that wine may cheer the heart of man.

segments.t: Ut edúcas panem de terra: * et vinum lætíficet cor hóminis:

content.latin: 103:15 Ut exhílaret fáciem in óleo: * et panis cor hóminis confírmet.
content.english: 103:15 That he may make the face cheerful with oil: * and that bread may strengthen man’s heart.

segments.t: Ut exhílaret fáciem in óleo: * et panis cor hóminis confírmet.

content.latin: 103:16 Saturabúntur ligna campi, et cedri Líbani, quas plantávit: * illic pásseres nidificábunt.
content.english: 103:16 The trees of the field shall be filled, and the cedars of Libanus which he hath planted: * there the sparrows shall make their nests.

segments.t: Saturabúntur ligna campi, et cedri Líbani, quas plantávit: * illic pásseres nidificábunt.

content.latin: 103:17 Heródii domus dux est eórum: * montes excélsi cervis: petra refúgium herináciis.
content.english: 103:17 The highest of them is the house of the heron. * The high hills are a refuge for the harts, the rock for the irchins.

segments.t: Heródii domus dux est eórum: * montes excélsi cervis: petra refúgium herináciis.

content.latin: 103:19 Fecit lunam in témpora: * sol cognóvit occásum suum.
content.english: 103:19 He hath made the moon for seasons: * the sun knoweth his going down.

segments.t: Fecit lunam in témpora: * sol cognóvit occásum suum.

content.latin: 103:20 Posuísti ténebras, et facta est nox: * in ipsa pertransíbunt omnes béstiæ silvæ.
content.english: 103:20 Thou hast appointed darkness, and it is night: * in it shall all the beasts of the woods go about:

segments.t: Posuísti ténebras, et facta est nox: * in ipsa pertransíbunt omnes béstiæ silvæ.

content.latin: 103:21 Cátuli leónum rugiéntes, ut rápiant, * et quærant a Deo escam sibi.
content.english: 103:21 The young lions roaring after their prey, * and seeking their meat from God.

segments.t: Cátuli leónum rugiéntes, ut rápiant, * et quærant a Deo escam sibi.

content.latin: 103:22 Ortus est sol, et congregáti sunt: * et in cubílibus suis collocabúntur.
content.english: 103:22 The sun ariseth, and they are gathered together: * and they shall lie down in their dens.

segments.t: Ortus est sol, et congregáti sunt: * et in cubílibus suis collocabúntur.

content.latin: 103:23 Exíbit homo ad opus suum: * et ad operatiónem suam usque ad vésperum.
content.english: 103:23 Man shall go forth to his work, * and to his labour until the evening.

segments.t: Exíbit homo ad opus suum: * et ad operatiónem suam usque ad vésperum.

content.latin: 103:24 Quam magnificáta sunt ópera tua, Dómine! * ómnia in sapiéntia fecísti: impléta est terra possessióne tua.
content.english: 103:24 How great are thy works, O Lord? * thou hast made all things in wisdom: the earth is filled with thy riches.

segments.t: Quam magnificáta sunt ópera tua, Dómine! * ómnia in sapiéntia fecísti: impléta est terra possessióne tua.

content.latin: 103:25 Hoc mare magnum, et spatiósum mánibus: * illic reptília, quorum non est númerus.
content.english: 103:25 So is this great sea, which stretcheth wide its arms: * there are creeping things without number:

segments.t: Hoc mare magnum, et spatiósum mánibus: * illic reptília, quorum non est númerus.

content.latin: 103:26 Animália pusílla cum magnis: * illic naves pertransíbunt.
content.english: 103:26 Creatures little and great. * There the ships shall go.

segments.t: Animália pusílla cum magnis: * illic naves pertransíbunt.

content.latin: 103:27 Draco iste, quem formásti ad illudéndum ei: * ómnia a te exspéctant ut des illis escam in témpore.
content.english: 103:27 This sea dragon which thou hast formed to play therein. * All expect of thee that thou give them food in season.

segments.t: Draco iste, quem formásti ad illudéndum ei: * ómnia a te exspéctant ut des illis escam in témpore.

content.latin: 103:28 Dante te illis, cólligent: * aperiénte te manum tuam, ómnia implebúntur bonitáte.
content.english: 103:28 What thou givest to them they shall gather up: * when thou openest thy hand, they shall all be filled with good.

segments.t: Dante te illis, cólligent: * aperiénte te manum tuam, ómnia implebúntur bonitáte.

content.latin: 103:29 Averténte autem te fáciem, turbabúntur: * áuferes spíritum eórum, et defícient, et in púlverem suum reverténtur.
content.english: 103:29 But if thou turnest away thy face, they shall be troubled: * thou shalt take away their breath, and they shall fail, and shall return to their dust.

segments.t: Averténte autem te fáciem, turbabúntur: * áuferes spíritum eórum, et defícient, et in púlverem suum reverténtur.

content.latin: 103:30 Emíttes spíritum tuum, et creabúntur: * et renovábis fáciem terræ.
content.english: 103:30 Thou shalt send forth thy spirit, and they shall be created: * and thou shalt renew the face of the earth.

segments.t: Emíttes spíritum tuum, et creabúntur: * et renovábis fáciem terræ.

content.latin: 103:31 Sit glória Dómini in sǽculum: * lætábitur Dóminus in opéribus suis:
content.english: 103:31 May the glory of the Lord endure for ever: * the Lord shall rejoice in his works.

segments.t: Sit glória Dómini in sǽculum: * lætábitur Dóminus in opéribus suis:

content.latin: 103:32 Qui réspicit terram, et facit eam trémere: * qui tangit montes, et fúmigant.
content.english: 103:32 He looketh upon the earth, and maketh it tremble: * he toucheth the mountains, and they smoke.

segments.t: Qui réspicit terram, et facit eam trémere: * qui tangit montes, et fúmigant.

content.latin: 103:33 Cantábo Dómino in vita mea: * psallam Deo meo, quámdiu sum.
content.english: 103:33 I will sing to the Lord as long as I live: * I will sing praise to my God while I have my being.

segments.t: Cantábo Dómino in vita mea: * psallam Deo meo, quámdiu sum.

content.latin: 103:34 Iucúndum sit ei elóquium meum: * ego vero delectábor in Dómino.
content.english: 103:34 Let my speech be acceptable to him: * but I will take delight in the Lord.

segments.t: Iucúndum sit ei elóquium meum: * ego vero delectábor in Dómino.

content.latin: 103:35 Defíciant peccatóres a terra, et iníqui ita ut non sint: * bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino.
content.english: 103:35 Let sinners be consumed out of the earth, and the unjust, so that they be no more: * O my soul, bless thou the Lord.

segments.t: Defíciant peccatóres a terra, et iníqui ita ut non sint: * bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Confessiónem et decórem índuit, amíctus lúmine sicut vestiménto.
content.english: Ant. He was clothed with honour and majesty, covering Himself with light as with a garment.

segments.t: Ant.
Confessiónem et decórem índuit, amíctus lúmine sicut vestiménto.

content.latin: ℣. Magna est glória eius in salutári tuo.
content.english: ℣. His glory is great in thy salvation.

segments.t: Magna est glória eius in salutári tuo.

content.latin: ℟. Glóriam et magnum decórem impónes super eum.
content.english: ℟. Honour and great majesty shalt Thou lay upon him.

segments.t: Glóriam et magnum decórem impónes super eum.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: Absolutio. A vínculis peccatórum nostrórum absólvat nos omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus.
content.english: Absolution. May the Almighty and merciful Lord loose us from the bonds of our sins.

segments.t: Absolutio.
A vínculis peccatórum nostrórum absólvat nos omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: Quóniam multa de perículis, multa de passióne sua, multa de morte et de cæde discipulórum locútus est Dóminus, et áspera complúra atque árdua eis iniúnxit; et illa quidem in præsénti vita, et iam imminébant; bona vero in spe et exspectatióne erant: ut puta, quia servárent ánimam suam, si pérderent eam; quia in glória Patris sui ventúrus sit, et prǽmia redditúrus: ut visu étiam certióres fáceret, et osténderet quidnam sit illa glória, cum qua ventúrus est, quantum cápere póterant in hac præsénti vita, illis osténdit eámque détegit, ne aut sua aut Dómini morte dóleant, et máxime Petrus.
content.english: Since the Lord had spoken much concerning dangers, much concerning His Own sufferings, much concerning death, and the killing of His disciples, and had laid upon them many hard and grievous things, and since all these were in this present life, and already hanging over them, whereas the good things were matter for hope and waiting as, for example, that whosoever should lose his life for His sake should find it, for that the Son of Man should come in the glory of His Father, and reward every man according to his works. Matth. xvi. 25, 27. Therefore, to assure them by their own eyes, and show them what the glory is wherein He will come, He manifested and unveiled it to them, as far as in this life they were able to grasp it, lest they and especially Peter should grieve over their own deaths, or the death of their Lord.

content.latin: Et vide quid agit, cum de regno et de gehénna disserúerit. Nam in eo quod dixit: Qui ínvenit ánimam suam, perdet eam; et quicúmque perdet eam grátia mei, invéniet ipsam; et in eo quod ait: Reddet unicuíque secúndum ópera sua; et regnum et gehénnam designávit. Cum ígitur de utrísque disserúerit, regnum quidem ut óculis cernátur, concédit, gehénnam autem mínime; quóniam rudióribus atque ineptióribus illud necessárium fuísset, sed, cum illi probi essent ac perspicáces, satis fuit eos a melióribus confirmári. Hoc étiam multo magis ipsum decébat. Non tamen omníno illud prætermísit, sed et aliquándo atrocitátem gehénnæ quasi ante óculos propónit, véluti cum Lázari imáginem descrípsit, et eius méminit qui denários centum repétiit.
content.english: Behold what He doth, when He treateth of heaven and hell. Where He saith Whosoever will save his life shall lose it, and whosoever will lose his life for My sake shall find it. And again He shall reward every man according to his works in these words He pointeth at heaven and hell. But although He speaketh concerning both, He giveth a glimpse of heaven only and not of hell. To see hell would have profited the brutish and stupid, but His disciples were upright and clear-sighted, and therefore for them it was enough to be strengthened by the better things. This was what suited Him the best. Yet He left not the other altogether undone. Sometimes He set the horrors of hell, as it were, before the eyes, as for instance in the parable of the rich man and Lazarus, and that of him who was fain to wring the hundred pence from his fellow-servant.

content.latin: Tu vero Matthǽi philosophíam consídera, qui non celávit nómina eórum qui præpósiti fúerant. Quod et Ioánnes sǽpius facit, cum exímias Petri laudes veríssime ac diligentíssime descríbat. Nullum enim in hoc Apostolórum consórtio livor aut inánis glória locum habébat. Primos ígitur Apostolórum seórsum assúmpsit. Quam ob rem eos solos accépit? Quia excellentióres céteris vidélicet erant. Cur autem non íllico, sed post sex dies hoc fecit? Ne céteri scílicet discípuli seu hómines moveréntur; qua de re nec eos nominávit, quos acceptúrus erat.
content.english: But mark well Matthew's good will, in not concealing the names of those who were preferred. John also likewise often recordeth the special praises of Peter with great truthfulness and care. For in this companionship of the Apostles, there was no envy, nor did vainglory find place. It was therefore the leaders of the Apostles whom Christ took apart from the others. And wherefore did he take these only? Because there were evidently superior to the rest. And why did he not do this straightway, and not until after six days? Evidently to spare the natural feelings of the other disciples; and for the same reason Christ did not for six days announce who were to go up.

content.english: 99:3 We are his people and the sheep of his pasture. * Go ye into his gates with praise, into his courts with hymns: and give glory to him.

segments.t: Pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius: * introíte portas eius in confessióne, átria eius in hymnis: confitémini illi.

content.latin: 99:4 Laudáte nomen eius: quóniam suávis est Dóminus, in ætérnum misericórdia eius, * et usque in generatiónem et generatiónem véritas eius.
content.english: 99:4 Praise ye his name: for the Lord is sweet, his mercy endureth for ever, * and his truth to generation and generation.

segments.t: Laudáte nomen eius: quóniam suávis est Dóminus, in ætérnum misericórdia eius, * et usque in generatiónem et generatiónem véritas eius.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

Resplénduit fácies eius sicut sol, vestiménta autem eius facta sunt alba sicut nix, allelúia.
